subject.title: [Feature]: Reusable gateway WebSocket client SDK package

question: Should OpenClaw publish and support a low-level `@openclaw/gateway-client` WebSocket SDK, route external apps only through the higher-level `@openclaw/sdk`, or keep the current Gateway RPC docs-only path for now?
rationale: Current main has private implementation groundwork, but publication would define a new external Gateway auth, pairing, scope, reconnect, transport, and support contract that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep This As The SDK Direction Packet
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported low-level client boundary before publishing it or redirecting it to the higher-level SDK track.

options.title: Fold Into App SDK Track
options.body: Close or redirect this only after maintainers decide the public external-client contract is solely the higher-level SDK/Gateway RPC path and preserve the low-level requirements there.

options.title: Sponsor Public Gateway Client Publication
options.body: Move toward publication with install docs, Node/browser support boundaries, security guidance, compatibility tests, and live Gateway pairing proof.

recommendation.title: Keep This As The SDK Direction Packet
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported low-level client boundary before publishing it or redirecting it to the higher-level SDK track.

likelyOwner.reason: The private package extraction and host-wrapper boundary most directly trace to steipete's merged gateway-client package work.
